Next year we hope to have the services of Joe Scamell in addition to some new members when our chances should be even better than this year.

In the 2 miles walk, Harry Churcher walked in fine style and eventually finished second to Joe Scamell, with George Oliver third. In the 300 yards, Alan Sexton was on scratch mark and duly qualified for the final by winning his heat.

On June 22nd we had our annual mob match with Surrey W.C. on the track at Tooting, beating them by 89 points to 121, with Joe Scamell (jr.), Brian Shepherd and Mac taking the handicap awards in that order.

Joe Scamell won a Veterans' mile handicap at Parliament Hill Fields on August 23rd off 22 yards. Bert East won the Veterans' A.C. 2 miles Championship and was second in the Erith Open Mile on August 7th.

It was pleasing to see young Joe Scamell walking so well again and hope this will continue during the track season. The handicap was deservedly won by Eric Hall (1.30) with Ron Fairman(16.00), 2nd, and Hugh McGreechan (0.40) 3rd.
We were pleased to see Gerry Warr and Joe Scamell junr. back on the track, they both just missed the seven miles but gave a glimpse of better things to come.

His many friends will be glad to know that Joe Scamell is making a good recovery after serious respiratory trouble. Joe joined us in 1920 and has continued to show his walking paces until as recently as a few months ago.
JOE SCAMELL and BEN KNIFTON joined Belgrave in 1925, and the following year TOM MORELL, CHARLIE JONES, ALF HARLEY and LEN ROLLINS were accepted into membership.

Helping to run the meeting as she has done for the last three years was Mrs Dunsford, who ensured that full details of each race were available within 15 minutes of the end of each race.

Ron is now finding himself in the most heavily populated part of the field, which will give him experience in picking off the opposition. It was good to see Joe Scamell out again. On his fourth lap he heard the patter of what were once tiny feet - his son Michael lapping him.
Of our others one was Joe Scamell, who by dint of hard work and training seems to actually enjoy racing. Unfortunately, Mike Nicholls battling well up the field was disqualified.

Mike Scamell and John Newnham are soon in and our hopes of retaining the team title look good, Steve Marshall, Mike Nicholls and Edie Crossingham are next home all under 50 mins. and then Martin Hills and Joe Scamell.

Congratulations to two Belgravians, Joe Scamell, at a modest 58, collected 3rd place in the Essex 50 kms, 4th man for Belgrave in the National 50 kms and then proceeded to complete the Hastings, and then the Brighton to finish in under 10 hours.

As the day wore on Joe Scamell was forced to retire leaving 4 on the road, Carl Lawton was about to retire at 40 miles, but was informed by Barbara Dunsford, ably manning the feeding station, that he was not and so it progressed.
Belgrave entered 12 for this event and for a change all 12 appeared, although Joe Scamell was sidelined with injury. Again Belgrave just came home ahead although it was close.
